prompt_text: Generate a 5-second worked-solution video differentiating y=(3x^2+1)^4 using the chain rule. Show the outer function, inner function, derivative steps, and final derivative without skipping the inner derivative.
expected_concepts: outer function power rule
inner function derivative
chain rule multiplication
final derivative 24x(3x^2+1)^3
expected_visual_elements: two labeled boxes: outer u^4 and inner u=3x^2+1
expected_narrative_order: Set u=3x^2+1 and identify outer function u^4.
Differentiate outer function to get 4u^3.
Differentiate inner function to get 6x.
Multiply dy/du by du/dx.
Substitute u back to obtain 24x(3x^2+1)^3.
pedagogical_target_audience: Undergraduate calculus students practicing symbolic differentiation
discipline_specific_rubric: Must show the inner derivative 6x, not just the outer power rule.
Final derivative must be 24x(3x^2+1)^3.
Notation must keep u, x, dy/du, and du/dx consistently distinguished.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 whiteboard opening frame. Top title: 'Chain rule'. Left side shows the problem in large readable math: y = (3x^2 + 1)^4. Center has two empty labeled boxes: 'inner u = ____' and 'outer y = ____'. Right side has a blank step list: 1) dy/du, 2) du/dx, 3) multiply. Do not show the final derivative yet.
avoid: showing final answer in opening frame
quality_checks: Opening frame makes the chain-rule decomposition visually auditable.
All formula text is large enough to read from a thumbnail.
The first frame sets up the solution without revealing it.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second educational video explaining RC circuit charging. Show a battery, resistor, capacitor, current direction, and a voltage curve approaching the battery voltage with the time constant tau=RC.
expected_concepts: capacitor voltage rises asymptotically
current is largest at the start and decreases over time
time constant tau equals R times C
after one time constant the capacitor reaches about 63 percent of final voltage
expected_visual_elements: current arrow that fades over time
capacitor voltage graph Vc(t) vs time
expected_narrative_order: Start with an uncharged capacitor connected through a resistor to a battery.
Show large initial current into the capacitor.
Draw the rising capacitor-voltage curve.
Mark tau=RC and the 63 percent point.
End with current reduced and capacitor nearly charged.
pedagogical_target_audience: Undergraduate introductory physics or circuits students
discipline_specific_rubric: Must not show capacitor voltage jumping instantly to battery voltage.
Must distinguish current decrease from voltage increase.
Graph must label tau=RC and the 63 percent point correctly.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 physics teaching diagram. Left: simple RC circuit with battery, switch open, resistor R, capacitor C initially uncharged. Label battery V, resistor R, capacitor C. Right: blank axes labeled time t and capacitor voltage Vc(t), with no curve drawn yet. A small text cue says 'After switch closes'.
avoid: completed charging curve in opening frame
quality_checks: The initial state is clearly before charging begins.
Circuit labels and graph axes are readable.
The frame supports later animation of both circuit and graph.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second educational video explaining an SN2 reaction with backside attack and inversion of configuration. Show hydroxide attacking bromomethane from the backside, bromide leaving, and the stereochemical inversion outcome.
expected_concepts: SN2 is concerted
nucleophile attacks from the backside
leaving group departs as the new bond forms
configuration inverts at the reactive carbon
expected_visual_elements: central carbon with leaving group Br
dashed and wedged bonds before and after
expected_narrative_order: Show substrate with leaving group and nucleophile on opposite side.
Animate backside attack arrow toward carbon.
Show transition state with partial C-O and C-Br bonds.
Show bromide leaving as C-O bond forms.
End with product geometry inverted.
discipline_specific_rubric: Must depict a single concerted step, not a carbocation intermediate.
Attack direction must be backside relative to the leaving group.
Product must show inversion of configuration rather than retention.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 organic chemistry mechanism board. Center: simple tetrahedral carbon with Br leaving group on the right and two generic groups shown as wedge and dash. Left: OH- nucleophile placed on the backside approach path, with an empty curved-arrow slot but no attack arrow yet. Add labels 'nucleophile' and 'leaving group'. Keep molecule large and uncluttered.
avoid: carbocation intermediate in the opening frame
quality_checks: The geometry makes backside attack possible to judge.
Chemical labels are readable and correctly placed.
The first frame sets up the mechanism without completing it.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second educational video explaining CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing from guide RNA matching a target DNA sequence to Cas9 cutting both strands, followed by either NHEJ disruption or HDR repair with a template.
expected_concepts: guide RNA base-pairs with target DNA
Cas9 makes a double-strand break
NHEJ can disrupt the gene
HDR can copy from a repair template
expected_visual_elements: split repair paths NHEJ and HDR
expected_narrative_order: Show guide RNA aligning to the target DNA.
Bring Cas9 to the matched site.
Show a double-strand cut.
Split into NHEJ and HDR repair paths.
Contrast disruption versus precise edit.
pedagogical_target_audience: Undergraduate biology students learning gene-editing mechanisms
discipline_specific_rubric: Must not imply guide RNA cuts DNA by itself; Cas9 performs the cut.
Must show double-strand break before repair.
Must distinguish NHEJ disruption from HDR template-guided repair.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 molecular biology diagram. Horizontal DNA strand across the center with a short highlighted target segment. Above it, guide RNA is aligned but not yet fully paired. A Cas9 icon sits nearby, not cutting yet. Right side has two empty branches labeled NHEJ and HDR for later. Use large simple labels, not tiny base letters.
avoid: showing DNA already cut in first frame
quality_checks: Opening frame clearly separates targeting from cutting.
Repair branches are visible but not filled yet.
Labels make the biology auditable from one frame.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second worked-solution video interpreting a simplified 12-lead ECG snippet to localize an inferior STEMI. Highlight ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, connect those leads to the inferior wall, and name the likely RCA territory while noting that full clinical context is needed.
expected_concepts: ST elevation in contiguous inferior leads
leads II, III, and aVF view the inferior wall
inferior STEMI is often RCA territory
ECG interpretation needs clinical context
expected_visual_elements: ST elevation visible in II, III, aVF
heart diagram with inferior wall shaded
expected_narrative_order: Show the 12-lead grid and the question.
Highlight ST elevation in II, III, and aVF.
Group these as contiguous inferior leads.
Shade the inferior wall on a heart diagram.
State likely RCA territory with clinical-context caveat.
discipline_specific_rubric: Must identify II, III, and aVF as inferior leads.
Must not call the pattern anterior or lateral STEMI.
Must include a clinical-context caveat rather than making a standalone diagnosis from video alone.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 clinical teaching whiteboard. Left: simplified 12-lead ECG grid with lead labels I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1-V6; leads II, III, and aVF show visibly raised ST segments but are not highlighted yet. Right: blank table with columns 'ECG evidence' and 'Localization', plus an unshaded heart outline.
must_include: raised ST segments in II, III, aVF
avoid: final STEMI label in opening frame
quality_checks: Inferior-lead evidence is visible enough to judge.
The answer is not already revealed.
Clinical tone is educational and non-alarming.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second worked-solution video running Dijkstra's algorithm from node A on a weighted graph. Update tentative distances, pop the minimum from a priority queue, relax edges, and end with the shortest distance to node E.
expected_concepts: Dijkstra uses nonnegative edge weights
tentative distances are updated by edge relaxation
the next node selected has minimum tentative distance
finalized nodes are not revisited
expected_visual_elements: weighted graph with nodes A through E
expected_narrative_order: Initialize A=0 and other nodes as infinity.
Push A into the priority queue.
Pop the current minimum node and relax outgoing edges.
Update the distance table and queue after each relaxation.
Finalize the shortest path distance to E.
pedagogical_target_audience: Undergraduate computer science students learning graph algorithms
discipline_specific_rubric: Must select nodes by current minimum tentative distance, not visual position.
Must keep distance-table values consistent across shots.
Must only use nonnegative edge weights and end with a correct shortest distance to E.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 algorithm whiteboard. Left: weighted graph with nodes A, B, C, D, E and readable edge weights: A-B 2, A-C 5, B-C 1, B-D 4, C-D 1, D-E 3, C-E 7. Right: blank distance table for A-E and an empty priority queue box. Mark source A with a small start label, but do not fill the table yet.
must_include: nodes A B C D E
edge weights A-B 2, A-C 5, B-C 1, B-D 4, C-D 1, D-E 3, C-E 7
avoid: filled final path in opening frame
quality_checks: All graph weights are legible and stable.
Workspace supports stepwise distance updates.
The first frame does not reveal the final distance.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second worked-solution video analyzing a negative supply shock in an AD-AS diagram. Shift short-run aggregate supply left, show output falling and price level rising, and distinguish this from a demand shock.
expected_concepts: negative supply shock shifts SRAS left
price level rises
real output falls
stagflation differs from demand-driven recession
expected_visual_elements: new equilibrium with higher P and lower Y
brief comparison note: not AD shift
expected_narrative_order: Show the initial AD-SRAS equilibrium.
Introduce a negative supply shock.
Shift SRAS left while keeping AD fixed.
Mark higher price level and lower output.
Name the result stagflation and contrast with AD shift.
pedagogical_target_audience: Undergraduate economics students studying aggregate demand and supply
discipline_specific_rubric: SRAS must shift left/up, not AD.
Price level must rise while output falls.
Must not label the result as ordinary demand-deficient recession.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 economics graph. Axes labeled Price level P and Real output Y. Draw one downward AD curve and one upward SRAS0 curve meeting at E0. Add an empty arrow placeholder near SRAS0 labeled 'supply shock?' but do not draw the shifted curve yet. Right side has blank result boxes: P: ____ and Y: ____.
must_include: blank P and Y result boxes
avoid: already-shifted SRAS curve in opening frame
quality_checks: Initial equilibrium is clear and uncluttered.
The first frame sets up a graph reasoning task.
Axes and curve labels are readable.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second worked-solution video sorting three constitutional changes into judicial review, statute, or constitutional amendment. Use examples: court strikes down a law, Congress passes a voting statute, and the text of the Constitution is formally changed.
expected_concepts: judicial review can invalidate laws
statutes are ordinary laws
constitutional amendments change constitutional text
the three processes have different actors and thresholds
expected_visual_elements: decision arrows from cards to columns
expected_narrative_order: Show three unsorted example cards.
Define the three process columns.
Move court strikes down law to judicial review.
Move Congress passes voting statute to statute.
Move formal text change to constitutional amendment.
discipline_specific_rubric: Must not confuse judicial review with constitutional amendment.
Must distinguish Congress passing a statute from changing constitutional text.
Must show states or ratification threshold for amendments at least briefly.

first_frame.prompt: Clean 16:9 civics sorting board. Three empty columns labeled Judicial review, Statute, Constitutional amendment. Below are three cards: 'Court strikes down a law', 'Congress passes voting law', 'Constitution text is changed'. Small actor icons for Court, Congress, and States sit near the columns. Do not sort cards yet.
quality_checks: The classification task is visible from the opening frame.
Each card has short readable text.
Actors are present without overcrowding the frame.

prompt_text: Generate a 5-second worked-solution video scanning the line 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?' as iambic pentameter. Mark unstressed and stressed syllables, group five iambs, and explain why the meter supports the line's rhythm.

pentameter has five feet
Shakespeare's line can be scanned as five iambs
meter analysis requires syllable-level evidence

Group syllables into five iambs.
Name iambic pentameter.
Connect the pattern to the line's rhythm.
